images.title: Bicycles and tricycles
images.purpose: Shows the 20 cycles with 46 wheels: 14 bicycles and 6 tricycles, each tricycle adding one wheel.
images.composition: Twenty simple cycle icons in two rows of ten in the centre, with the equation underneath.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, generous empty margins, the main object large and centred. Two rows of ten simple flat cycle icons, evenly spaced. Each icon is a short straight bar with small wheel circles under it. Row 1: ten bicycles, teal (#0072B2) bar with 2 wheels each. Row 2: the first four are bicycles like row 1; the last six are tricycles, amber (#E69F00) bar with 3 wheels each, the third wheel filled reddish purple (#CC79A7). Under the 14 bicycles, one brace with 14 bicycles; under the 6 tricycles, one brace with 6 tricycles. Below, centred: 3t + 2(20 − t) = 46 and to its right t = 6. Exactly 20 icons, 14 bicycles with 28 wheels and 6 tricycles with 18 wheels, 46 wheels in all; no riders, no road.

images.takeaway: Each tricycle adds one wheel to 40, so 6 tricycles.
images.description: Shows the 20 cycles with 46 wheels: 14 bicycles and 6 tricycles, each tricycle adding one wheel.
images.context: 20 bicycles would have 40 wheels; 46 − 40 = 6 extra wheels, so 6 tricycles; check 18 + 28 = 46.

image_decisions.why: Counting the cycles and the extra wheels in one picture links the story to its equation.
